findings.summary: Accepted with high confidence: for arbitrary finite-alphabet broadcast channels, the averaged UV scalar formed from separately optimized upper concave envelopes satisfies B_avg(W₁×W₂)=B_avg(W₁)+B_avg(W₂), even with correlated product-channel inputs and joint envelope auxiliaries. This does not establish additivity of the complete UV region, common-joint-(U,V) formulations, arbitrary weighted scalarizations, the simplified GK functional, or the full Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem 9 bound.

Accepted with high confidence: receiver-skew symmetry implies B_br(W)=B_avg(W), and the optimization may be restricted to invariant input laws. The result follows by covariance of the two scalar branches and concavity under symmetrization; it does not extend the separately relaxed rows to a simultaneous common-(U,V) formulation or establish equality for nonsymmetric channels.

Accepted with high confidence: for every finite product of receiver-skew-symmetric finite-alphabet broadcast channels, B_br(∏ᵢWᵢ)=∑ᵢB_br(Wᵢ). This follows from preservation of skew symmetry under products, branch-average equality, and exact additivity of B_avg, without a hidden product-input restriction.

Accepted with high confidence: for the half-skew BSSC P, B_br(P)=B_avg(P)=2h₂(1/4)−5/4=0.3725562489182657…, and for every finite n both scalars on P^{×n} equal n(2h₂(1/4)−5/4). The specialization correctly uses receiver symmetry and the sharp posterior-support calculation, including the equality-achieving posterior mixture.

Accepted: 2h₂(1/4)−5/4 is a valid branchwise-relaxed UV sum-rate converse, but it is not achievable-rate evidence and does not improve the governed BSSC capacity interval. Its value exceeds both the benchmark upper endpoint 0.369316568803963 and the supplied continuously certified full-Theorem-9 bound 0.369296945969202842443, so it changes neither capacity frontier.
